## Description

Let's create the main structure of the website with semantic elements. Design a simple layout with a header, main section, and a footer. We have provided you with the Figma designs for this page. Pay attention to the CSS rules and the elements in the designs. The element names are the names of the tags you need to use. Some elements have IDs next to them: `anchor: #nav-brand`. The tag name is `anchor` and the ID is `nav-brand`.

Moreover, note the element structure in Figma; it hints at your HTML element structure. The design of the elements should resemble Figma designs. You can adjust the position of the elements however you like.

The `anchor` links don't need to redirect anywhere, and they shouldn't have any `text-decoration`.

You can play around with the colours of the elements.

## Example

![landing page basic layout](https://ucarecdn.com/e29e311c-4ba6-47e4-b9e8-fb23a3746d3d/)
title: Layout

## Description

Time to add some information about your amazing product/service prices. Add two new sections inside the `main` tag. The first section will feature a title and a text; the second section will be more peculiar.

In most frontend libraries, there is a component called `card` that presents a neat way to show content on websites. Take the [Bootstrap](https://getbootstrap.com/docs/5.2/components/card/#example) library as an example. In the second section, build similar cards and show the prices of your product/service. Pay attention to the CSS rules and the elements in the designs. The element names are the names of the tags you must use. You might notice that some elements have different naming principles than in the previous stage, such as `div: .card`. Here, the tag name is `div`, and the class is `card`.

You can choose to write what you like for the text content for these sections. There should be three cards in the second section.

Align the text content of these cards in the second section and the `h1` and the paragraph in the first section to the `center`.

Not only that, but you can also play around with the colors of the elements.

## Example

![landing page product card](https://ucarecdn.com/9c705d85-1231-44f0-b6bb-28483c768dc6/)
title: Prices

## Description

Since you have various pricing plans for your product/service, you need to put a comparison table to show the differences between these plans. This stage will feature a new section inside the `main` tag. This new section will have another title and a table. For the details of this new section, refer to the designs. Pay attention to the CSS rules and the elements in the designs. The element names are the names of the tags you must use. The naming principles from the previous stages still apply.

You can choose to write what you like for the text content of the table. It needs to have at least **5 rows and 4 columns**. The `td` and `th` tags in the table should have `1px` and `solid` borders.

Align the new `h2` text to `centre`.

You can play around with the colors of the elements.

## Example

![landing page cards and tables](https://ucarecdn.com/5236bfaf-a783-49e2-8d98-13411045bc85/)
title: Compare plans

## Description

Now that you've added all the content you need, it's time to make the website responsive for mobiles. In this stage, your website should readjust itself for mobile screens. In the Figma designs, you will see two different views: one for desktop and one for mobile. Pay attention to the screen widths and the placements/positions of the elements.

Pay attention to the CSS rules and the elements in the designs. The element names are the names of the tags you must use. The naming principles from the previous stages still apply.

You can adjust the position of the elements however you like.

## Example
